title: Semantics of a positive two-argument oracle call
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program, $O$ an oracle family, $x$ an input bit string, and $G$ a guard on configurations. Suppose the instruction at state $l$ calls oracle $j$ in whole-input mode with the two registers $r,s$, branching to $l_1$ on a true answer and to $l_0$ on a false answer. For register values $v$ and any proposition $P$, if $G$ holds at $(l,v,\mathrm{none})$ and $O_j$ answers true on $\langle x,\langle\operatorname{bits}(v(r)),\operatorname{bits}(v(s))\rangle\rangle$, then terminating semantics and acceptance equivalent to $P$ at $(l_1,v,\mathrm{none})$ imply the same at $(l,v,\mathrm{none})$.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at $l$ is the stated whole-input call to oracle $j$ with registers $r,s$ and branches $l_1,l_0$
The successor configuration $(l_1,v,\mathrm{none})$ has terminating semantics and acceptance equivalent to $P$
